MIT: Keep its copyright line and license text with the code.
Apache-2.0: Keep its copyright line and license text with the code.
MPL-2.0: Keep its copyright line and license text with the code.
GPL-2.0-only: Keep its copyright line and license text with the code.

MIT: The copied files stay Apache-2.0: keep the license, the NOTICE lines and a note of what you changed. Your project becomes MIT and Apache-2.0.
Apache-2.0: Keep the license, carry its NOTICE lines into yours, and say what you changed.
MPL-2.0: The copied files stay Apache-2.0, with their NOTICE lines and a note of what you changed.
GPL-2.0-only: Apache-2.0's patent terms are extra restrictions GPL-2.0 does not allow.
GPL-3.0: GPL-3.0 was written to accept Apache-2.0 code. The combined work is GPL-3.0.
AGPL-3.0: AGPL-3.0 accepts Apache-2.0 code. The combined work is AGPL-3.0.

MIT: File-level copyleft: the copied files stay MPL-2.0 and their source must stay available. Your other files keep your license.
Apache-2.0: File-level copyleft: the copied files stay MPL-2.0 and their source must stay available. Your other files keep your license.
MPL-2.0: Keep the notices, and keep the source of changed MPL files available.
GPL-2.0-only: Allowed unless the files are marked 'Incompatible With Secondary Licenses'.
GPL-3.0: Allowed unless the files are marked 'Incompatible With Secondary Licenses'.
AGPL-3.0: Allowed unless the files are marked 'Incompatible With Secondary Licenses'.

MIT: Distributing it would make the whole work GPL-2.0. Only if you relicense your project.
Apache-2.0: Distributing it would make the whole work GPL-2.0, which cannot take Apache-2.0 terms.
MPL-2.0: Distributing it would make the whole work GPL-2.0.
GPL-2.0-only: Same license. Keep the notices and share the source when you distribute.
GPL-3.0: 'Only' means no later version: GPL-2.0-only and GPL-3.0 cannot be combined.
AGPL-3.0: 'Only' means no later version: GPL-2.0-only cannot be combined with AGPL-3.0.

MIT: Distributing it would make the whole work GPL-3.0. Only if you relicense your project.
Apache-2.0: Distributing it would make the whole work GPL-3.0. Only if you relicense your project.
MPL-2.0: Distributing it would make the whole work GPL-3.0.
GPL-2.0-only: GPL-3.0 code cannot go into a GPL-2.0-only work.
GPL-3.0: Same license. Keep the notices and share the source when you distribute.
AGPL-3.0: Section 13 of both licenses allows combining them. The combined work is AGPL-3.0.

MIT: The whole work would become AGPL-3.0, including offering the source to users over a network.
Apache-2.0: The whole work would become AGPL-3.0, including offering the source to users over a network.
MPL-2.0: The whole work would become AGPL-3.0.
GPL-2.0-only: AGPL-3.0 code cannot go into a GPL-2.0-only work.
GPL-3.0: Section 13 allows combining them, but the AGPL part keeps its network clause.
AGPL-3.0: Same license. Offer the source of your modified version to everyone who uses it, including over a network.

MIT: No license means no permission. Ask the author, or write your own.

GPL-2.0-only: No license means no permission. Ask the author, or write your own.
